subtitle: A freed Habshi master of men, letters and land in the Deccan twilight

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle hero wide inside a bustling Deccan court
panels.action: Malik Ambar stands in richly woven robes beneath Khadki’s arches, surrounded by Brahmin clerks, Maratha chiefs and Habshi guards, as a Persian scroll unfurls from his hand over a map of the Deccan.

dialogue.text: In Khadki’s crowded court, a man once sold as a slave rules as Peshwa—Malik Ambar, the Habshi whose Persian letters teach princes the grammar of kingship in a fractured Deccan.

i18n.hi: खड़की के भीड़ भरे दरबार में, कभी बिक चुका आदमी पेशवा बनकर राज करता है—मलिक अम्बर, वो हब्शी जिसकी फ़ारसी चिट्ठियाँ राजकुमारों को बादशाही का व्याकरण सिखाती हैं टूटे-फूटे दकन में।

panels.shot: slow push-in from above onto the growing town of Khadki
panels.action: Bird’s-eye view of Khadki: new houses and markets clustering around a fortified palace, dusty lanes packed with traders, soldiers and scribes moving like threads around Malik Ambar’s seat.

dialogue.text: By 1608, Khadki swells from a small settlement into a humming capital. At its center stands Malik Ambar, former Habshi slave, now de facto ruler of Ahmadnagar’s shattered kingdom.

i18n.hi: १६०८ तक आते‑आते खड़की एक छोटी बसाहट से गूंजती राजधानी बन जाती है। उसके बीचोंबीच मलिक अम्बर खड़ा है—पूर्व हब्शी ग़ुलाम, अब अहमदनगर की टूटी हुई रियासत का असल हाकिम।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Ambar seated in durbar
panels.action: Malik Ambar sits on a modest but elevated seat in the audience hall, back straight, eyes sharp, as attendants usher in Deccani nobles and clerks clutching bundles of paper.

dialogue.text: The Nizam Shahi sultan’s authority is thin, Mughal armies press from the north, and yet in this hall decisions of war, tax and land flow through Malik Ambar’s hands.

i18n.hi: निज़ाम शाही सुल्तान की ताक़त पतली है, मुग़ल फ़ौजें उत्तर से चढ़ती हैं, फिर भी इसी हॉल में जंग, लगान और ज़मीन के फ़ैसले मलिक अम्बर के हाथों से बहते हैं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Malik Ambar’s hand writing
panels.action: Close on Malik Ambar’s weathered hand guiding a reed pen across creamy paper, lines of flowing Persian script appearing beside a small seal and a careful date.

dialogue.text: His power is not only on horseback. It lives in letters and firmans, composed in Persian, where this Habshi commander speaks in the polished idiom of elite Indo-Persian politics.

i18n.hi: उसकी ताक़त सिर्फ़ घोड़े की पीठ पर नहीं। वो रहती है चिट्ठियों और फ़रमानों में, फ़ारसी में लिखी हुई, जहाँ ये हब्शी सरदार आलीशान हिंद‑फ़ारसी सियासत की सधी ज़बान में बोलता है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of a letter being composed
panels.action: From behind Malik Ambar, we see a letter addressed to a prince taking shape; a scribe listens as Ambar dictates and gestures toward a map spread beside him.

dialogue.text: Write: “Justice must bind our officers as firmly as obedience binds our soldiers.”

i18n.hi: लिखो: “इंसाफ़ हमारे अफ़सरों को उतनी ही मज़बूती से बाँधे, जितनी फ़रमाबरदारी हमारे सिपाहियों को बाँधती है।”

panels.shot: medium shot of Ambar with mixed council around a table
panels.action: Malik Ambar stands at a low table covered with account books; a Brahmin revenue expert, a Maratha chief and a Muslim officer lean in while Habshi guards watch the doorway.

dialogue.text: In council he gathers Brahmin revenue men, Maratha horsemen, Deccani Muslims and Habshi captains—different tongues, scripts and gods bound by the needs of land, pay and defense.

i18n.hi: मजलिस में वो ब्राह्मण महसूलदार, मराठा घुड़सवार, दकनी मुसलमान और हब्शी सरदारों को जुटाता है—अलग ज़ुबानें, लिपियाँ और ख़ुदा, मगर ज़मीन, मेहनताना और रक्षा की ज़रूरत से बंधे हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot highlighting Ambar’s posture of authority
panels.action: Low angle from the floor shows Malik Ambar pointing decisively to a revenue ledger, his face calm but firm, while a hesitant noble listens with lowered eyes.

dialogue.text: He bears the title Peshwa, a Deccan office of chief minister and military head. Through it, a freed slave commands old titles and new loyalties without erasing his origin.

i18n.hi: वो पेशवा का ख़िताब उठाए है—दकन का वज़ीर‑ए‑आज़म और फ़ौजी सरदार। इसी ओहदे से एक आज़ाद ग़ुलाम पुराने ख़िताबों और नई वफ़ादारियों पर हुक्म चलाता है, बिना अपनी जड़ मिटाए।

panels.shot: wide shot of court audience with envoys and petitioners
panels.action: A crowded durbar hall: village headmen in simple cotton, nobles in brocade, foreign envoys and scribes wait as Malik Ambar hears petitions from the edge of his dais.

dialogue.text: Surviving documents speak in workaday language of land shares, arrears, discipline. Behind them lie fields and forts whose people seldom see this room but feel its orders.

i18n.hi: बची काग़ज़ात की ज़ुबान रोज़मर्रा की है—ज़मीन के हिस्से, बाक़ाया, अनुशासन। इनके पीछे वो खेत और क़िले हैं, जिनके लोग इस कमरे को शायद ही देखें, पर इसके हुक्म ज़रूर महसूस करें।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ambar listening to a village representative
panels.action: Malik Ambar leans slightly forward, listening as a weary village representative gestures about drought-struck fields, while a clerk waits with his pen poised above a register.

dialogue.text: “Assess with fairness,” he instructs, “but the treasury must not run dry.”

i18n.hi: “तौलो तो इंसाफ़ से,” वो हुक्म देता है, “पर ख़ज़ाना सूखने न पाए।”

panels.action: Overhead view of a large map of the Deccan on the floor; Malik Ambar moves counters marking forts and Mughal camps, his officers watching intently.

dialogue.text: Even as he refines revenue, his letters carry instructions for campaigns, alliances and scorched-earth tactics that frustrate Mughal generals like Jahangir’s son, the prince Khurram.

i18n.hi: राजस्व सँवारते‑सँवारते उसकी चिट्ठियाँ जंग, गठजोड़ और जला‑डाला ज़मीन की चालें भी ले जाती हैं, जो मुग़ल सरदारों को लाचार करती हैं—जहाँगीर के बेटे, शहज़ादे ख़ुर्रम समेत।

panels.shot: close-up of Ambar reading a hostile missive
panels.action: Malik Ambar stands by a window, holding an ornate Mughal letter; his eyes narrow as we glimpse words with insults about his African origin and former bondage.

dialogue.text: Mughal chroniclers spit at him as an upstart Habshi slave. In their prose, his skin and past are weapons. In his own documents, he answers with commands, not complaints.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल इतिहासकार उसे उछलू हब्शी ग़ुलाम कहकर थूकते हैं। उनकी नثر में उसका रंग और अतीत ही हथियार हैं। उसकी अपनी दफ़्तरी ज़ुबान में जवाब सिर्फ़ हुक्म हैं, शिकवे नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ambar dictating a firm reply
panels.action: Back in his study, Malik Ambar dictates calmly to a scribe as guards stand ready; behind him hangs a simple standard of the Nizam Shahi state.

dialogue.text: “Write that the Deccan will be defended. Let them measure me by results.”

i18n.hi: “लिखो कि दकन का बचाव होगा। मुझे नतीजों से तौलें।”

panels.shot: wide courtyard shot showing military drill and bureaucracy side by side
panels.action: In Khadki’s courtyard, soldiers train with spears while, under a shaded veranda, clerks copy revenue orders and store scrolls into chests.

dialogue.text: His state rests on coercion and extraction—soldiers must be paid, forts provisioned, villages assessed. Talent governs, but hierarchy, fear and force hold this experiment together.

i18n.hi: उसकी रियासत ज़बरदस्ती और वसूली पर टिकी है—सिपाहियों को तनख़्वाह चाहिए, क़िलों को राशन, गाँवों को आँकना पड़ता है। हुनर हुकूमत करता है, पर दर्जा, ख़ौफ़ और ज़ोर इस तजुर्बे को जोड़े रखते हैं।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of Ambar in private reflection
panels.action: At night, Malik Ambar sits alone by a low oil lamp, a few earlier letters spread before him, his gaze distant and thoughtful.

dialogue.text: “From bondage to this desk of kings—yet I, too, command chains.”

i18n.hi: “ज़ंजीर से इस बादशाहों की मेज़ तक—और आज भी ज़ंजीरें मेरे ही हुक्म से चलती हैं।”

panels.shot: wide shot of Khadki’s growth over time, slightly time-lapse feel
panels.action: A sequence-like wide view: new wells, mosques, temples and markets rise around Khadki’s core, suggesting years of rule and urban expansion under Malik Ambar’s administration.

dialogue.text: Through years of siege and negotiation, Khadki grows. His mixed court leaves its imprint: routinized tax, Persian chancery, Deccan titles woven into everyday government.

i18n.hi: घेराबंदियों और मोलभाव के सालों में खड़की फ़ैलती जाती है। उसका मिला‑जुला दरबार अपनी छाप छोड़ता है—पक्का लगान, फ़ारसी दफ़्तर, दकनी ओहदे रोज़मर्रा की हुकूमत में गुँथे हुए।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of aging Ambar at his desk
panels.action: An older Malik Ambar sits heavier at the same desk, beard streaked with white, signing a document as younger officers watch, aware that they are inheriting routines he built.

dialogue.text: By the 1620s, age creeps into his frame, but the system he fashioned outlives him. Accounts, orders and offices continue even as bodies and faces change.

i18n.hi: १६२० के दशक तक उम्र उसके जिस्म में उतरने लगती है, मगर बनाया हुआ निज़ाम उससे आगे जीता है। हिसाब, हुक्म और दफ़्तर चलते रहते हैं, चाहे चेहरे और जिस्म बदलते रहें।

panels.shot: wide shot of Khadki after Ambar, showing continuity and change
panels.action: After his time, Khadki’s palace remains busy; different banners fly, but scribes still write in Persian and officers still use titles once tied to Malik Ambar’s hand.

dialogue.text: Later rulers and empires claim this machinery, adjusting it to their needs. The memory of the Habshi Peshwa becomes a story, but his bureaucratic habits become a norm.

i18n.hi: बाद के बादशाह और सल्तनतें इसी मशीनरी को अपनाकर अपनी ज़रूरत से ढालते हैं। हब्शी पेशवा की याद क़िस्सा बन जाती है, मगर उसकी दफ़्तरी आदतें उसूल बन जाती हैं।

panels.shot: symbolic shot of a single letter preserved in an archive-like setting
panels.action: A single fragile letter bearing Malik Ambar’s seal lies carefully preserved on a wooden tray, light falling on its faded script as unseen hands hold it in study.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars read his surviving letters to princes and officers. In their lines, they hear an African freedman fully fluent in the language of Deccan rule.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद उलेमा और विद्वान उसके बचे हुए ख़त पढ़ते हैं—शहज़ादों और अफ़सरों को लिखे। उन लकीरों में उन्हें एक आज़ाद अफ़्रीकी सुनाई देता है, जो दकनी हुकूमत की ज़ुबान में पूरा माहिर है।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up on Ambar’s face dissolving into the map of the Deccan
panels.action: Close on Malik Ambar’s steady, unsmiling face that slowly blends into a textured map of the Deccan covered in routes and place-names he once ordered.

dialogue.text: Malik Ambar’s court shows how power can rise from bondage when skill and will find openings—yet even then, dignity grows within the hard frame of hierarchy, not outside it.

i18n.hi: मलिक अम्बर का दरबार दिखाता है कि कैद से भी ताक़त उठ सकती है, जब हुनर और हिम्मत को रस्ते मिलें—पर तब भी इज़्ज़त दर्जे की सख़्त सीढ़ी के भीतर ही बढ़ती है, उससे बाहर नहीं।

title_i18n.en: The Court of a Freed Slave

subtitle_i18n.en: A freed Habshi master of men, letters and land in the Deccan twilight
subtitle_i18n.hi: आज़ाद हब्शी जो इंसान, इल्म और ज़मीन का मालिक है, दकन की सांझ में
